title: Trump's Alien 'Disclosure Speech' Rumours Grow Despite White House Saying No Such Address Is Planned
excerpt: Rumours that Donald Trump could announce evidence of extraterrestrial life have spread online, despite the White House saying no such speech is planned. Declassified UAP files remain under review.
content:
Rumours that President Donald Trump could announce evidence of extraterrestrial life have intensified across UFO forums and social media, despite the White House saying that no such speech is planned.

The speculation has grown in the United States amid an unusually public period of UAP-related activity in 2026, as the government continues to release declassified records on unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP.

Trump directed the Secretary of War and other relevant departments and agencies on Feb. 19 to begin identifying and releasing government files related to extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs.

The Department of War subsequently published five releases through its Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, known as PURSUE. The fifth release was published Aug. 7.

The department says additional files will be released on a rolling basis.

Trump Alien Speech Claims Lack Proof

The central claim is straightforward, if extraordinary, some UAP advocates believe Trump has been given, or could soon deliver, a prepared speech stating that the US government possesses evidence of non-human intelligence.

No public evidence has established that such a speech exists.

According to reports, a White House spokesperson stated via email that "no such speech is planned." The spokesperson added that the administration would continue to release files as they become available, allowing the public to evaluate the information.

The statement provides the White House's clearest publicly reported position on the claim.

The reports have nevertheless gathered momentum among advocates who see the document releases as a prelude to something larger. They point to Trump's Feb. 19 directive ordering the identification and release of government files related to extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs.

The Department of War describes PURSUE as an interagency effort involving the White House, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and several other federal agencies. The public archive includes UAP-related documents, images and videos, but does not state that the released records establish the existence of extraterrestrial life.

On social media and in some UFO-focused podcasts, individual records have been interpreted by advocates as possible evidence of a broader disclosure. The government's release of unresolved material, however, does not by itself establish that the incidents involved extraterrestrial activity.

What the PURSUE Files Show

The modern UAP debate has been shaped by a shift in official language. The Pentagon has acknowledged and investigated unexplained incidents, while Congress has held public hearings involving military personnel, intelligence veterans and other witnesses.

But an unexplained case is not the same as evidence of extraterrestrial visitors. The archive includes records of unresolved UAP incidents, their inclusion does not by itself establish extraterrestrial activity.

The fifth PURSUE release contained 41 files, 22 documents, 16 videos and three images, according to the archive. Some records date back decades, while others concern more recent events. The files are available for public review, but they do not amount to a presidential confirmation of life beyond Earth.

Some former officials and UAP advocates have argued that public hearings, government investigations and congressional interest have reduced the stigma surrounding reports of unexplained phenomena. Those claims concern the changing public debate, not proof that the phenomena are extraterrestrial.

Critics have pointed to the long history of unverified disclosure claims. Claims of imminent UAP disclosure have circulated for decades without a publicly verified presidential announcement confirming extraterrestrial life.

Robert Bigelow's Reported Proposal

The latest rumours also gained traction after reports involving businessman Robert Bigelow. According to reports, Bigelow had given Trump a proposed line acknowledging a non-human presence on Earth.

There is no public confirmation that Trump adopted the wording or plans to make such a statement.

Available reports do not establish that Trump accepted the proposal, adopted its wording, or plans to make a similar statement.

An alleged private conversation, even one involving a prominent supporter of UAP research, would not by itself constitute an official policy announcement.

The administration's publicly announced UAP initiative is the identification and release of government records. The Department of War says it is continuing to publish material through PURSUE, with additional releases expected.

For now, the Trump alien disclosure speech remains an unverified claim. The PURSUE files and the government records-release programme are real. The White House told WIRED that no such speech is planned.
